**Published online:**
Sep 2, 2026

**Geographic focus:**
Global — primary focus on US, with notable coverage of Japan, New Zealand, UK, Australia, Middle East (Iran/Strait of Hormuz)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps recent data (JOLTS, ISM, NZ rate decision, US airstrikes on Iran)
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Fed Sep 15–16 meeting, upcoming jobs report (Friday), CPI data, BOJ rate decision this month
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

**Synopsis:**
Renewed US-Iran military hostilities are pushing oil prices sharply higher (Brent ~$95, WTI ~$90), stoking inflation fears and lifting US 10-year yields to ~4.81% — their highest since Nov 2023. This is reinforcing USD strength and driving market expectations for a Fed rate hike at the Sep 15–16 meeting to 68% (up from ~40% a week prior). Fed Governor Barr and Fed Chair Warsh (Jackson Hole) have both signaled openness to hikes if inflation persists. The yen remains pressured above 160/USD despite joint US-Japan intervention rhetoric; further coordinated FX action appears unlikely while oil stays elevated due to Strait of Hormuz tensions.

---

**Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?**
Relevance: YES — Core themes are US yields, Fed rate hike probability, USD dynamics, and macro data impacting rate expectations.

**Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 90 (strongly YES)
Probability of increase: 68% (as per CME FedWatch cited in the article for September meeting)

**Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?**
Relevance: 10 (marginally — only implicitly, as the baseline before recent repricing)
Probability of holding: 32%

**Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 0 (NO — cuts are not mentioned or implied anywhere)
Probability of decrease: 0%

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: +75 (Decidedly more hawkish than before) — The combination of geopolitical oil shock, rising 10-year yields to 4.81%, Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole signals, Gov. Barr's hawkish Tuesday remarks, and market repricing to 68% hike probability all point firmly in a hawkish direction with no offsetting dovish signals present in the article.
